newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australia-Taiwan bagasse project in doubt.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australia-Taiwan bagasse project in doubt.

text.p: A A$250 million Australia-Taiwan sugar cane bagasse project proposed for the Australian state of Queensland has been thrown into doubt by one of two Australian partners declining to take up equity in the venture.
The decision leaves state-run Taiwan Sugar Corp and privately-owned Perth-based Queensland Bagasse undecided on whether the project will go ahead.
Ron Swindells, chief executive officer of Mackay Sugar Co-operative Association, said on Wednesday that his group had decided not to take up equity participation in the project.
Bagasse is the fibrous cane waste left after the extraction of sugar juice in the milling process. It is used in the manufacture of paper and building materials such as wallboard.
Contacted by Reuters, Taiwan Sugar declined to comment on whether it had decided not to proceed with the project, as reported by The Australian Financial Review newspaper on Tuesday.
But Peter Derrett, principal of Queensland Bagasse, described the project as "very robust", with the partners still close.
"We believe in the fullness of time that the project will happen," he told Reuters.
Queensland Bagasse and Taiwan Sugar both have 40 percent of the proposed project, while a 20 percent stake had been offered to Mackay Sugar, Derrett said.
Taiwan Sugar was to have assisted with export sales of bagasse pulp, which is used to make fine-quality paper.
Mackay Sugar already faced major expansion through a A$100 million expansion of sugar milling capacity over 10 years, Swindells said. "We want to devote our resources to that."
The bagasse project would be worth between A$180 million and A$250 million, depending on final itemisation of figures, he said.
It was to have been financed by a combination of debt and equity.
